correctness.rationale: A direct spanning-tree/edge-increment bijection counts all compatible colorings on any finite connected cactus exactly; cycle-block constraints are disjoint, so articulation vertices create no false independence. The independently published circulation theorem gives the exact activity from these block windings. Closed-cycle state-current conservation proves the factor-three CCA/GHM relation. For bouquets, exact near-endpoint trinomial coefficients give p_n ~ (6/s!) n^s 3^{-n} and q_n ~ (6/(s+3)!) n^{s+3}3^{-n}; independent petals yield a Poisson maximal count and concentration on the two top rates. Every one of the configurations on nine small test cacti was checked under both transition rules; finite checks support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest identified theorems of Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff (2016/2018), Theorem 3, and Doba (2018), Section 7, determine rates pointwise from cycle densities. They are not claimed as new. Neither inspected source reports a uniform-coloring rate distribution across all cactus graphs, independent modular cycle-block counts, or the sharp residue-dependent two-clock Poisson saturation window for exponentially many attached cycles. The manuscript proves those extra assertions. Exact priority cannot be guaranteed by finite searches, so unindexed equivalents remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: A prior cactus modular-flow coefficient enumeration or a rare-maximal-winding limit could be indexed under probabilistic combinatorics rather than excitable automata; searches cannot rule it out.
The general maximum-cycle-circulation theorem subsumes the pointwise rate identity, so originality is confined to the exact all-coloring distribution and critical two-rate extreme-value limit.
The 1995 paper was read in relevant introductory portions, not exhaustively page-by-page; its stated infinite-line parameter regime is not directly comparable.

value.rationale: The exact distribution over all colorings, rather than a pointwise criterion, is a natural invariant of excitable networks. It is solved for every finite connected cactus graph with arbitrary cycle sizes and bridges, and provides direct synchronization populations. The nontrivial large-network consequence is a sharp residue-sensitive trichotomy among the scales 3^n, 3^n/n and 3^n/n^2, with a two-rate Poisson crossover. This precise saturation threshold is motivated by maximal allowed circulation and is not an arbitrary slice or a small numerical improvement.
